source_text: Quam legem etiam peccati in Prophetis et Apostolis iam magno morum et signorum fulgore conspicuis et post illam gratiam mysteriorum Christi, quam tu his omnibus dogmatis tui flagitiis opitulari putas, mansisse et viguisse deiuras.
pass_a_gloss: Which law also of sin you swear remained and flourished in the Prophets and Apostles already conspicuous by the great brightness of manners and signs, and after that grace of the mysteries of Christ which you think assists all these outrages of your dogma.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: You swear that this law of sin remained and flourished even in the prophets and apostles, already illustrious through the great brilliance of their conduct and miracles, and even after the grace of Christ’s mysteries—which you suppose comes to the aid of all these outrages of your doctrine.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: The law of sin in the body.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
